results.title: AI: Artificial Intelligence | EPOCHS IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS  | Facebook
results.content: Understanding epochs in large language models. EPOCHS IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS. Understanding Epochs in Large Language Models (LLMs). In machine learning, particularly during the training phase of a neural network, an epoch refers to one complete pass through the entire training dataset. For LLMs, this means the model has seen (and had the opportunity to learn from) all tokens in the dataset once during that epoch. If your dataset has 1 trillion tokens, one epoch means the model processes those 1 trillion tokens in some order, possibly shuffled. 2. Why Epochs Matter in LLM Training. Too few epochs → underfitting (model hasn’t learned enough patterns). Too many epochs → overfitting (model memorizes rather than generalizes). The learning rate schedule often depends on epochs, with warmup and decay phases tied to them. Every epoch has a proportional compute cost. For massive datasets, even a single epoch can take weeks on large GPU clusters. ● Epoch: Entire dataset processed once. For LLMs, steps are often more useful than epochs for scheduling learning rates because datasets can be terabytes in size, making “epochs” an infrequent milestone. 4. Epochs in Large-Scale LLM Training. In traditional ML, 50–200 epochs might be common for small datasets. We rarely train for many full epochs — even 1–3 epochs can be enormous. ● Token sampling techniques (like temperature-based sampling or curriculum learning) sometimes replace strict epoch definitions. 5. Overfitting Risks in Multiple Epochs. ● Even 2–3 epochs can risk memorization of rare data points (e.g., personal info). Use less than a full epoch, but repeat high-quality subsets more often (known as data curation weighting). 6. Epoch Scheduling in LLMs. LLM training rarely uses a fixed number of epochs from the start; instead:. ● Warmup period: A small fraction of the first epoch gradually increases learning rate. ● Decay phase: Learning rate decreases over later epochs. ● Early stopping: Halt training if validation loss plateaus, even mid-epoch. Epoch = full dataset pass, but in LLMs this is often a massive computation. ● For smaller datasets, epochs help track progress; for LLMs, total tokens processed is often the more meaningful metric. ● Over-training (too many epochs) risks overfitting and memorization.
